dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The recharge data shows 17 annual-plan (365-day) renewals having a total of $1,506.29 from dealers DLR-104 and DLR-219."
"DLR-104's May batch contained 8/8 accepted rows, with 0 duplicate IDs and $0 reconciliation difference."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Their effective dates fall between 1 May and 28 May, while all were posted on 31 May."
"This pattern is consistent with the stated dealer submission process rather than evidence of fabricated or duplicated revenue."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Manipulated reporting — not supported."
"Whether the 90 annual renewals actually activated subscriber entitlements"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not reverse or reclassify the 31 May revenue."

"As a reversible control, separately flag the 17 annual renewals when presenting weekly trends, and obtain the DealerDrop entitlement-posting result for the two May batches before fully closing the review."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue. It is a normal month-end dealer-upload process, rather than duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, or a demonstrated pipeline defect."
"annotate the weekly trend pack as a month-end dealer batch/timing effect"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No material issue" is somewhat broader than the evidence because entitlement activation was not actually tested and duplicate cash impact was not independently demonstrated beyond the stated reconciliation results.

"No duplicate source_event_id values exist in the recharge dataset" rules out exact source-ID duplication but does not by itself rule out duplicate cash, duplicate customer entitlement, or other economic duplication.
"The same month-end batching pattern is also visible in the import log for March and April" is asserted without identifying the specific batches, rows, or dates supporting that comparison.
The email-based explanation is treated as corroboration, but the submission does not provide a precise email passage or independently verify the dealer permission beyond the described process.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the principal alternatives—duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and a pipeline defect—well, especially the possibility of a recurring posting-time process. The main alternative still unresolved is a provisioning or entitlement issue: accepted imports and ledger reconciliation do not prove that every renewal activated exactly one subscriber entitlement. A related unresolved possibility is duplicate cash or economic duplication not captured by source_event_id uniqueness.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and document a reproducible matched check for all 17 flagged renewals—and preferably all 90 West annual renewals—covering one-to-one entitlement activation and duplicate cash/ledger impact, using source_event_id plus account and transaction identifiers; then retain the event-time reporting correction regardless of the result.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Only 94/2,709 (3.5%) Nova-S1 sessions created a CareDesk case, versus 222/442 (50.2%) under legacy."

"South CareDesk cases declined from 184 in April to 104 in June." | Source: tickets.csv; "Nova-S1 had 507 errors (18.7%), including 302 authentication errors and 205 issue-menu errors." | Source: ivr_interactions.jsonl

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "NovaIVR also introduced a large number of sessions that ended in authentication/technical errors or abandonment before a CareDesk case could be created."
"The email explicitly states that the containment dashboard begins only after subscriber identification, while sessions ending before authentication are reported elsewhere."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The South decline is entirely caused by NovaIVR” — not established."
"We need to know whether they successfully resolved their issue elsewhere, retried later, called through another channel, or simply failed to get help."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."

"Keep NOVA-S1 running as pilot for southern regin but don't hurry to expand nationally yet. track all ivr sessions including pre-authentication errors and abandonments and also and measure repeat contact and confirmed issue resolution per IVR attempt."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Person: Farah Iqbal, Customer Care Operations, because she owns IVR journey stages, case-creation conditions, and the containment definition."
"What exact conditions cause Nova-S1 to create a CareDesk case, and did those conditions change between the legacy IVR and Nova-S1?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "2,709 South NOVA-S1 IVR sessions occurred after the 10 May pilot start, but only 98 sessions reached the self_service terminal stage." This claim is not separately represented in the evidence table, and the relationship between 98 self_service sessions and 94 case-creating sessions is not explained.

"NovaIVR also introduced a large number of sessions that ended in authentication/technical errors or abandonment before a CareDesk case could be created." The cited aggregates show errors and abandonment, but do not by themselves establish that every such session was eligible for or would otherwise have created a case.

"South had 30 service events in May and June, so operational conditions also changed during the pilot period." Thirty service events establish occurrence, but not whether conditions improved, worsened, differed from other regions, or explain the case decline.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the key benign alternative that abandoned or errored customers may have resolved their issue through another channel or on a later attempt, rather than assuming all abandonment was dissatisfaction. It also preserved the possibility that continuing service incidents or other operational factors contributed to the South decline. However, it did not test demand mix, seasonality, or a comparable-region alternative in detail.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a reproducible regional and time-based comparison showing the South case break around 10 May alongside service-event exposure and IVR stage outcomes, then link failed sessions to subscriber-level repeat contacts and confirmed resolution. This would distinguish missing case capture from genuine experience improvement and strengthen the causal assessment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, all four rows, for `cleared=yes`, `impact_mw=0`, and durations of 1–7 minutes.
It separately cites all four rows for the distinct inverter IDs and event types, and distinguishes observed contents from the inference that escalation is not justified.
The qualification “Confidence: high for the observed file contents, not for overall plant health” appropriately limits the evidence claim.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests the common-inverter/common-event hypothesis against four distinct inverters and four distinct event types rather than treating the event count alone as a pattern.
It recognizes that the four-row export may be incomplete and proposes checking for status filters and a wider date range.

The reasoning does not substantially test a specific innocent mechanism, such as a transient communications or telemetry issue, and does not use event timestamps or event-specific fields to discriminate mechanisms.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission states high confidence only in what the supplied file shows, and low confidence about events outside the export.
It says “the file alone does not justify escalation” rather than claiming that overall plant health is proven.
It identifies the smallest relevant uncertainty—export completeness—and proposes a read-only check before closing the review.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and run one simple completeness check” follows from zero impact, cleared status, short duration, and lack of recurrence.
The proposed read-only export “without status filters” for 27 May–4 June, with a possible 30-day recurrence check, is proportionate and discriminating.
The conditional close criterion—no additional open, nonzero-impact, or recurring events—preserves a sensible operational safeguard.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly stops short of inventing a plant problem from four brief, self-cleared, zero-impact events.
It accurately scopes the conclusion by saying alarm labels alone do not prove equipment failure and that escalation should resume only if broader data shows recurrence or an ongoing problem.
This matches the supplied evidence and appropriately treats the mixed warning/info wording as insufficient by itself for escalation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “No Operational issues found” is broader than the evidence supports; the export supports only that no operational impact is shown in these four records, not that plant health is established.

“Alarming telemetry warning labels” and the reference to “active inverter damage” are not clearly established as the actual event mechanism; the submission appropriately rejects that inference, but could state more explicitly that the event semantics remain unknown.
The claim that “the overall All 4 events” were the complete relevant set is not established; the later completeness-check recommendation correctly acknowledges this limitation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: These may be transient communications or telemetry-quality events rather than inverter equipment faults; the zero MW impact, short durations, self-clearing, and lack of recurrence support that possibility, but the supplied export does not establish the mechanism. The mixed warning/info labels merit only a low-priority data-quality or event-semantics check.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Use the event timestamps and event-specific reason/type fields, if available, to check whether the warning and info records share a communications or telemetry signature; this would discriminate a benign transient from an equipment-related event without escalating on the current evidence.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies dispatch_blocks.csv, the dsm_penalty_rs field, and exact daily totals for 28 and 29 May.
It cites the 12 pilot_revision and 84 qca_base blocks and explicitly describes the same-day base-versus-submitted shadow calculation.
It distinguishes the DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf observation that settlement depends on accepted schedule, meter data, and deviation bands from causal interpretation.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission notices that the 31.6% comparison uses different days and that 28 May was the highest-penalty day in the extract.
It tests innocent explanations including differing wind, generation, operating conditions, and settlement mechanics.
It rejects both fabrication and causal-certainty hypotheses for stated evidentiary reasons, while retaining the smaller same-day modeled effect.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The wording 'does not prove that the pilot caused the saving' and 'does not remove possible effects from wind, operating conditions or hindsight' appropriately limits the causal claim.
The submission labels arithmetic confidence separately from causal confidence and identifies the unknown split between pilot effect and day-to-day variation.
It specifies decision-changing evidence: repeated comparable events, immutable pre-submission timestamps, matched blocks, complete settlement data, and net commercial value.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to 'keep the pilot at its current scope and hold wider expansion' preserves operational value without treating weak causal evidence as proof.
The proposed read-only shadow calculation is reversible and uses a contemporaneous normal recommendation as a counterfactual.
The next test compares accepted schedule, actual generation, deviation, penalty, and net commercial value across repeated matched events, with clear expand/stop criteria.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion credits the reproducible 31.6% arithmetic reduction but rejects attributing the full amount to the pilot.
It reports the smaller 17.6% same-day modeled benefit as potential rather than proven causal savings.
It reaches the appropriately scoped conclusion that the pilot may have value but requires repeated controlled evidence before expansion.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase 'a real and reproducible 31.6% drop' is supported as an arithmetic settlement reduction, but 'real' could be misread as a causal performance effect; the submission immediately narrows and corrects that interpretation.

The 17.6% same-day result is described as a modeled potential rather than an observed causal saving. Its validity still depends on the counterfactual penalty calculation and complete settlement inputs, which the submission appropriately flags as requiring verification.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Most or all of the 31.6% cross-day improvement could reflect differences in wind, generation, operating conditions, or settlement context rather than the pilot. The evidence nevertheless supports a smaller, provisional same-day modeled benefit, so the correct alternative is not 'the pilot has no value' but 'its incremental value remains unestablished.'
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide the explicit block-level formula and inputs used to calculate the 29 May base_schedule_mw counterfactual penalty, then repeat that same contemporaneous comparison across several matched high-wind or stow events using immutable pre-submission timestamps.

"Declaration: P1001 declared with 90211000."
"Schema omits system/version/date/ruling authority."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Any different string proves there is an error”: Rejected because the Swiss reference uses 90211000 and says that Swiss and EU strings do not always have to match."
"I also cannot say that 90211000 is definitely the wrong code."
"The supplied EU tariff matrix is not enough to establish the Swiss rule."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The code mismatch is real but we can say yet that the customs declaration is wrong."
"The materials do not prove that 90211000 is an incorrect Swiss declaration code."
"we need to check the correct Swiss code and the rules that applied on that date before deciding."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Both share HS6 902110; local suffixes differ."
"Helios 90211090 is commercial ERP data."
"add the jurisdiction, version, and date to the comparison."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Ask the customs team to verify the correct Swiss code before changing the declaration."
"Put the mapping on hold for now and ask for confirmation of the tariff classification or ruling."
"Escalate only if it conflicts with 90211000. Otherwise, close the false positive"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Switzerland is the destination, not the product's origin" is directionally supported by the AWB and the invoice/declaration, but the AWB alone establishes shipment destination/consignee context rather than proving the complete origin analysis.

"The Swiss reference uses 90211000 and says that Swiss and EU strings do not always have to match" is asserted from the supplied tariff materials but would be stronger with an exact row or passage quoted.

"This keeps both options open while checking the only legal fact that is still unclear" overstates the situation: product-specific classification facts, the legal status of the reference data, and the applicable Swiss tariff source may also remain unclear.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The mismatch could still reflect an incorrect Swiss declaration, an outdated or incorrectly mapped Helios product-master value, or a product-specific classification issue. The submission appropriately leaves these possibilities open, but does not test them beyond requesting a Swiss tariff source or ruling.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly compare the product's technical description and classification attributes against the applicable Swiss tariff entry or binding ruling for 4 November 2025, while separately validating whether Helios 90211090 is an ERP mapping code rather than a Swiss customs code.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31 and marked ‘Expired in register’; the shipment date is 2025-09-18."
"The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`; the packet manifest lists six files and no shipment-specific supplier declaration."
"IE-2025-000411 declares P1006 with Preference=Yes, United States origin, 0.0% duty, and 90211090."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference=Yes proves the claim.’ — Rejected."
"‘US manufacturing origin proves the preference claim is false.’ — Rejected."
"‘The expired SUP-02 entry is enough.’ — Rejected."
"This points to an evidence gap, not proof of a false claim."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The Irish preference claim is not proven, so it should be held rather than cleared as preferential."
"Unsupported does not mean false. Verdict: unsupported, not disproved."
"Not finding a linked record does not prove that the claim is false, because the reference materials warn that supporting documents may exist outside the supplier register."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`."
"The commercial invoice also states United States as P1006's manufacturing country ... but the workshop says manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preference."
"Both origin-workshop.md and supplier_declaration_reference.txt warn that the supplier register may not contain every supporting document."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof."
"Do not clear the shipment as preferential until the evidence is verified."
"The supplied declaration shows 0.0% duty, so the hold is reversible. Do not assume any duty change until the tariff and preference treatment have been confirmed."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The packet confirms ... manufacturing origin" is slightly overstated: the packet records the invoice's stated manufacturing country, but that document alone does not independently establish the actual manufacturing origin.

"A valid link to SUP-03/05/06 plus supporting proof could support preference" is directionally reasonable, but those supplier-country entries do not by themselves establish eligibility under the applicable preference rule; the rule-specific qualification and complete origin evidence must also be verified.
"A US/non-qualifying supplier would support non-preferential treatment" depends on the supplier's actual sourcing and the governing rule, not merely the supplier's identity or location.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Valid shipment-specific preference evidence may exist outside the six-file packet or outside the supplier register; the missing linkage is therefore a control and evidence-retrieval gap rather than evidence that the declaration is false. Conversely, if Procurement confirms a non-qualifying sourcing route or cannot produce rule-compliant proof, the preference claim should be removed or corrected.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the evidence request explicitly rule-based: obtain the purchase order or supplier invoice linking the shipment to its supplier, the current supplier declaration, and the applicable preference rule and qualification records, then state precisely what evidence would establish or reject eligibility.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "For the 220 completed rows, the mean receipt-to-release time is 45.5 hours" and "lab-complete-to-release proxy is 26.9 hours mean / 21.3 hours median," tied to specific fields in batch_release.csv.
"185 of 262 rows (70.6%) have a qcore_release_ts of exactly 02:10:00," triangulated with source_freshness.csv and the QCore snapshot time.
The submission explicitly distinguishes the SOP-required evidence-available start from the available receipt and lab-complete timestamps, while labeling the latter as a proxy.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The repeated 02:10:00 release time is another warning sign" and "these timestamps may represent the snapshot rather than the actual release time," separating a timestamp/interface mechanism from apparent cycle performance.
The submission considers multiple mechanisms: missing evidence-available timestamps, snapshot/interface timing, and exclusion of open HOLD items.
It proposes a live-system check to discriminate whether 02:10 is an artifact or a genuine release time, although it does not fully reconcile the non-coherent timing of all joined extracts.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The analyst uses claim-specific confidence labels, including "High" for directly calculated fields and "Medium-High" for non-routine signals.
"This needs to be checked in the live system" and "We cannot calculate the true routine KPI" appropriately bound conclusions to missing timestamps and possible interface artifacts.
The submission acknowledges that missing/index-pending COA may reflect source delay rather than a confirmed release issue, but it could more explicitly quantify the impact of mixed extract snapshots.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Hold the KPI launch; the brief needs to be reframed" directly changes the decision rather than accepting the headline metric.
It recommends a small, reversible, read-only spot-check of 5–10 batches before dashboard publication and explains how results would determine whether the existing KPI can be supported.
It preserves useful operational analysis—"useful for understanding the queue"—while preventing an unsupported SOP KPI from being published.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects "The 1.5-day headline shows the real process speed" using both KPI-definition mismatch and the 02:10 concentration.
It rejects both the overreaction that "the extract is corrupt" and the unsafe action that "We can safely launch the dashboard now."
It states what future evidence could revive the timestamp interpretation: if actual live disposition times match 02:10, confidence in the timestamps increases.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: The highest-value next evidence is prioritized as a "small read-only spot-check of 5–10 batches in QCore and CertVault" to confirm evidence-upload and disposition times.
The table connects each unknown to a specific evidence source and explains how the result would change the decision.
The request is targeted rather than a generic demand for more data, while tracking the 42 HOLD rows is identified as a separate follow-up for survivorship-bias assessment.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the reported 1.5 days is "actually" 45.5 hours is unclear without an explicit reconciliation of how the Operations headline was calculated or rounded.

The claim that "the time calculations themselves are valid" is somewhat too broad because mixed-source freshness and interface-commit semantics may affect joined calculations, even if the arithmetic is correct.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent delay may reflect genuine workflow time, particularly evidence or disposition delays, rather than primarily a snapshot artifact. The current data cannot distinguish this from interface-timestamp delay without event-level or live-system audit timestamps.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly test point-in-time consistency across QCore, LabTrack, and related extracts, alongside obtaining an event/decision timestamp definition or event log; this would prevent a KPI decision based on a join of non-coherent snapshots and distinguish workflow delay from interface timing.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 24 open requests total $166,495.60..." — cites all 24 rows, quantity, quoted price, and status in part_requests.csv.
"Revision-B VLV-3722 has only 2 free units..." — triangulates spare_parts.csv, part_requests.csv, and part_restrictions.csv.
"The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June..." — cites source_freshness.csv and spares_transfer_policy.md.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "An exact MPN match works for all 13 populated MPN requests..." distinguishes retrieval from transfer eligibility.
"The main checks are not about finding more search results; they are about whether the part is actually eligible to move." tests identity, revision, qualification, reservation, and UOM constraints.
Rejected hypotheses address direct transfer, family interchangeability, and interpretation of negative availability.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Local CMMS is live, so current stock must be confirmed before calling a transfer actionable."
"Needs check" is used for identity ambiguity, insufficient clean stock, competing allocation, and revision mismatch.
"-1 is a verification flag... not proof of zero stock" appropriately avoids treating a negative availability value as definitive.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not turn raw search results into automatic transfers." provides an operational safeguard.
Separates "$20.5k" actionable candidates, "$64.2k" requiring verification, and "$81.7k" restricted.
Recommends live stock confirmation before confirmed transfer, although the label "actionable now" is somewhat stronger than the stale-snapshot evidence supports.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every search result can be transferred directly: Rejected" using reserved critical-asset stock and zero stock evidence.
"Parts from the same family can be used interchangeably: Rejected" using the VLV-3722 revision-A versus revision-B conflict.
"available_qty_global=-1 means there is no stock: Rejected" using on-hand quantities and the maintenance email.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: The table requests manufacturer part number and revision, live CMMS reservation/availability checks, and evidence concerning different revisions.
"If stock is available and unreserved..." explicitly links the requested evidence to a changed decision.
The requests are prioritized around the key uncertainties rather than asking generically for more data, though the final revision item is incomplete in the submission.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The main remaining matching problem" is master-data cleanup, and "search recall is not the main issue," are plausible but not fully demonstrated: exact MPN coverage for 13 requests does not establish that semantic normalization has little incremental value for the 11 requests lacking MPNs.

The classification of 8 requests as "Actionable now" is stronger than the evidence supports while the global stock snapshot is stale and the submission itself says live CMMS confirmation is still required. They are better characterized as high-priority candidates pending current availability and reservation confirmation.

The claim that all 13 populated-MPN requests have exact candidates is cited at file level but would be stronger with request-level joins, including explicit revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and freshness fields for each candidate.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may still provide material value for the 11 requests without clear part numbers, even if exact MPN matching is sufficient for the 13 populated-MPN requests. The evidence supports using semantic search as candidate generation rather than concluding that it is generally unnecessary; the unresolved issue is whether normalized descriptions can recover valid identities without creating unsafe equivalence assumptions.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a request-level live CMMS validation for the 8 proposed actionable transfers, recording current free quantity, reservation/criticality, revision, UOM, and qualification, while separately measuring semantic-search recall on the 11 no-MPN requests against maintenance-record-confirmed manufacturer part numbers. This would both validate the immediate value claim and test whether semantic search adds value beyond exact MPN joins.
